// This is your Prisma schema file,
// learn more about it in the docs: https://pris.ly/d/prisma-schema

generator client {
  provider = "prisma-client-js"
}

// Note that some adapters may set a maximum length for the String type by default, please ensure your strings are long
// enough when changing adapters.
// See https://www.prisma.io/docs/orm/reference/prisma-schema-reference#string for more information
datasource db {
  provider = "postgresql"
  url      = env("DATABASE_URL")
}

model Session {
  id                   String   @id
  shop                 String
  state                String
  isOnline             Boolean
  scope                String?
  expires              DateTime?
  accessToken          String
  userId               BigInt?
  firstName            String?
  lastName             String?
  email                String?
  accountOwner         Boolean?
  locale               String?
  collaborator         Boolean?
  emailVerified        Boolean?
  refreshToken         String?
  refreshTokenExpires  DateTime?
}

model ZipCode {
  id        String   @id @default(cuid())
  shop      String
  zipCode   String
  label     String?
  zone      String?
  message   String?
  eta       String?
  type         String   @default("allowed")
  isActive     Boolean  @default(true)
  codAvailable Boolean?
  returnPolicy String?
  createdAt    DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt DateTime @updatedAt

  @@unique([shop, zipCode])
}

model DeliveryRule {
  id            String   @id @default(cuid())
  shop          String
  name          String
  zone          String?
  zipCodes      String?  // comma-separated zip codes, or empty for "all in zone"
  minOrderAmount Float?
  deliveryFee   Float?
  freeShippingAbove Float?
  estimatedDays String?
  cutoffTime    String?  // e.g. "14:00" — orders after this go next day
  daysOfWeek    String?  // e.g. "Mon,Tue,Wed,Thu,Fri"
  isActive      Boolean  @default(true)
  priority      Int      @default(0)
  createdAt     DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt     DateTime @updatedAt

  @@index([shop])
}

model WaitlistEntry {
  id        String   @id @default(cuid())
  shop      String
  name      String?
  email     String
  zipCode   String
  note      String?
  status    String   @default("waiting") // waiting, accepted, rejected, notified, converted
  createdAt DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt DateTime @updatedAt

  @@unique([shop, email, zipCode])
  @@index([shop])
}

model WidgetConfig {
  id                    String  @id @default(cuid())
  shop                  String  @unique
  // Layout
  position              String  @default("inline") // inline, floating, popup
  // Colors
  primaryColor          String  @default("#008060")
  successColor          String  @default("#008060")
  errorColor            String  @default("#D72C0D")
  backgroundColor       String  @default("#FFFFFF")
  textColor             String  @default("#202223")
  // Text
  heading               String  @default("Check Delivery Availability")
  placeholder           String  @default("Enter your zip code")
  buttonText            String  @default("Check")
  successMessage        String  @default("Great news! We deliver to your area.")
  errorMessage          String  @default("Sorry, we don't deliver to this area yet.")
  notFoundMessage       String  @default("We currently do not ship to this ZIP code.")
  // Features
  showEta               Boolean @default(true)
  showZone              Boolean @default(false)
  showWaitlistOnFailure Boolean @default(false)
  showCod               Boolean @default(true)
  showReturnPolicy      Boolean @default(true)
  showCutoffTime        Boolean @default(true)
  showDeliveryDays      Boolean @default(true)
  blockCartOnInvalid    Boolean @default(false)
  blockCheckoutInCart   Boolean @default(false)
  showSocialProof       Boolean @default(true)
  // Border
  borderRadius          String  @default("8")
  // Custom CSS
  customCss             String?

  createdAt DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt DateTime @updatedAt
}

model Subscription {
  id                    String    @id @default(cuid())
  shop                  String    @unique
  planId                String    @default("free")
  billingInterval       String    @default("monthly")
  shopifySubscriptionId String?
  status                String    @default("active")
  trialEndsAt           DateTime?
  createdAt             DateTime  @default(now())
  updatedAt             DateTime  @updatedAt
}

model ShopSettings {
  id                String   @id @default(cuid())
  shop              String   @unique
  defaultBehavior   String   @default("block") // "block" = block all unlisted zips, "allow" = allow all unlisted zips
  notificationEmail String?  // email to receive waitlist notifications
  createdAt         DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt         DateTime @updatedAt
}

import type { HeadersFunction, LoaderFunctionArgs } from "react-router";
import { useNavigate, useRouteError } from "react-router";
import { authenticate } from "../shopify.server";
import { boundary } from "@shopify/shopify-app-react-router/server";
import {
  Page,
  Layout,
  Card,
  BlockStack,
  InlineStack,
  Text,
  Button,
  List,
  Divider,
  Box,
  Banner,
  Badge,
} from "@shopify/polaris";

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Loader — auth only, no data needed
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

export const loader = async ({ request }: LoaderFunctionArgs) => {
  await authenticate.admin(request);
  return {};
};

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Component
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

export default function HelpPage() {
  const navigate = useNavigate();

  const faqs: Array<{ question: string; answer: string }> = [
    {
      question: "How many ZIP codes can I add?",
      answer:
        "Depends on your plan. Free: 20 allowed ZIP codes. Starter: 500. Pro+: Unlimited.",
    },
    {
      question: "Can I restrict delivery to specific products?",
      answer:
        "Product-level ZIP rules are coming soon. This feature will let you restrict delivery for specific products to certain ZIP codes. Stay tuned for updates!",
    },
    {
      question: "How does the waitlist work?",
      answer:
        "Customers enter their ZIP if delivery isn't available, and you can notify them when you start delivering.",
    },
    {
      question: "Can I customize the widget colors?",
      answer:
        "Yes, go to Widget Customization and choose colors that match your brand.",
    },
    {
      question: "What if I need more help?",
      answer: "Contact support or check our documentation.",
    },
  ];

  return (
    <Page
      title="Help & Support"
      subtitle="Resources and answers to help you get the most out of Zip Code Checker"
      backAction={{ onAction: () => navigate("/app") }}
    >
      <Box paddingBlockEnd="1600">
        <Layout>

          {/* ----------------------------------------------------------------
              Section 1: Setup Guide
          ---------------------------------------------------------------- */}
          <Layout.Section>
            <Card>
              <BlockStack gap="600">
                <Text as="h2" variant="headingMd">
                  Setup Guide
                </Text>
                <Text as="p" tone="subdued" variant="bodyMd">
                  Follow these steps to get Zip Code Checker fully working on your storefront. The widget uses Shopify Theme App Extensions — no code changes required.
                </Text>

                {/* ---- A. Add the widget ---- */}
                <BlockStack gap="300">
                  <Divider />
                  <Text as="h3" variant="headingSm">
                    A. How to Add the Widget to Your Store
                  </Text>
                  <Text as="p" tone="subdued" variant="bodyMd">
                    The widget is a native Theme App Extension block. You add it directly inside the Shopify Theme Editor with no code required.
                  </Text>
                  <List type="number">
                    <List.Item>
                      Go to your Shopify Admin, then <Text as="span" fontWeight="semibold">Online Store → Themes</Text>.
                    </List.Item>
                    <List.Item>
                      Click <Text as="span" fontWeight="semibold">Customize</Text> on your active theme.
                    </List.Item>
                    <List.Item>
                      In the left sidebar, click <Text as="span" fontWeight="semibold">App Embeds</Text> and toggle on <Text as="span" fontWeight="semibold">Zip Code Checker</Text>.
                    </List.Item>
                    <List.Item>
                      Navigate to the page where you want the widget to appear (for example, a Product page).
                    </List.Item>
                    <List.Item>
                      Click <Text as="span" fontWeight="semibold">Add block</Text>, then under the Apps section select <Text as="span" fontWeight="semibold">Zip Code Checker</Text>.
                    </List.Item>
                    <List.Item>
                      Drag the block to your preferred position, then click <Text as="span" fontWeight="semibold">Save</Text>.
                    </List.Item>
                  </List>
                </BlockStack>

                {/* ---- B. Cart page validation ---- */}
                <BlockStack gap="300">
                  <Divider />
                  <InlineStack gap="200" align="start" blockAlign="center">
                    <Text as="h3" variant="headingSm">
                      B. How to Enable Cart Page Validation
                    </Text>
                    <Badge tone="attention">Pro Feature</Badge>
                  </InlineStack>
                  <Text as="p" tone="subdued" variant="bodyMd">
                    Cart validation blocks the checkout button when a customer has an unserviceable ZIP code. It requires the Pro plan and the Cart Validator block in your theme.
                  </Text>
                  <List type="number">
                    <List.Item>
                      In the Zip Code Checker app, go to <Text as="span" fontWeight="semibold">Widget Settings</Text>.
                    </List.Item>
                    <List.Item>
                      Enable the <Text as="span" fontWeight="semibold">Block checkout in cart for unserviceable ZIP codes</Text> toggle. This requires a Pro plan or higher.
                    </List.Item>
                    <List.Item>
                      Open your Shopify Theme Editor and navigate to the <Text as="span" fontWeight="semibold">Cart page</Text> template.
                    </List.Item>
                    <List.Item>
                      Click <Text as="span" fontWeight="semibold">Add block</Text>, then under the Apps section select <Text as="span" fontWeight="semibold">Cart Validator</Text>.
                    </List.Item>
                    <List.Item>
                      Click <Text as="span" fontWeight="semibold">Save</Text>. The cart will now block checkout for customers with an unvalidated or invalid ZIP code.
                    </List.Item>
                  </List>
                  <Banner tone="warning">
                    <Text as="p" variant="bodySm">
                      If the toggle is greyed out, upgrade to the Pro plan first from the Pricing page.
                    </Text>
                  </Banner>
                </BlockStack>

                {/* ---- C. How it works ---- */}
                <BlockStack gap="300">
                  <Divider />
                  <Text as="h3" variant="headingSm">
                    C. How It Works
                  </Text>
                  <Text as="p" tone="subdued" variant="bodyMd">
                    Understanding the flow helps you troubleshoot and explain the experience to customers.
                  </Text>
                  <List type="bullet">
                    <List.Item>
                      Customer enters their ZIP code on the product page — the result is saved in their browser session.
                    </List.Item>
                    <List.Item>
                      When the customer navigates to the cart page, the Cart Validator block reads the saved result.
                    </List.Item>
                    <List.Item>
                      If the ZIP was invalid or unserviceable, the checkout button is disabled and a warning banner is shown.
                    </List.Item>
                    <List.Item>
                      If the ZIP was valid, everything works normally and checkout proceeds as usual.
                    </List.Item>
                    <List.Item>
                      The session result is cleared when the customer checks out or starts a new browsing session.
                    </List.Item>
                  </List>
                </BlockStack>

              </BlockStack>
            </Card>
          </Layout.Section>

          {/* ----------------------------------------------------------------
              Section 2: Common Questions
          ---------------------------------------------------------------- */}
          <Layout.Section>
            <Card>
              <BlockStack gap="400">
                <Text as="h2" variant="headingMd">
                  Common Questions
                </Text>
                <Divider />
                {faqs.map((faq, index) => (
                  <BlockStack key={faq.question} gap="200">
                    {index > 0 && <Divider />}
                    <Text as="p" variant="bodyMd" fontWeight="semibold">
                      {faq.question}
                    </Text>
                    <Text as="p" tone="subdued" variant="bodyMd">
                      {faq.answer}
                    </Text>
                  </BlockStack>
                ))}
              </BlockStack>
            </Card>
          </Layout.Section>

          {/* ----------------------------------------------------------------
              Section 3: Support Hours
          ---------------------------------------------------------------- */}
          <Layout.Section variant="oneHalf">
            <Card>
              <BlockStack gap="400">
                <InlineStack align="start" gap="200">
                  <Text as="h2" variant="headingMd">
                    Support Hours
                  </Text>
                </InlineStack>
                <Divider />
                <BlockStack gap="200">
                  <InlineStack align="space-between">
                    <Text as="p" variant="bodyMd" fontWeight="semibold">Monday - Friday</Text>
                    <Text as="p" variant="bodyMd">9 AM - 6 PM IST</Text>
                  </InlineStack>
                  <InlineStack align="space-between">
                    <Text as="p" variant="bodyMd" fontWeight="semibold">Saturday</Text>
                    <Text as="p" variant="bodyMd">10 AM - 4 PM IST</Text>
                  </InlineStack>
                  <InlineStack align="space-between">
                    <Text as="p" variant="bodyMd" fontWeight="semibold">Sunday</Text>
                    <Text as="p" tone="subdued" variant="bodyMd">Closed</Text>
                  </InlineStack>
                </BlockStack>
                <Banner tone="success">
                  <Text as="p" variant="bodySm">
                    We typically respond within 2-4 hours during business hours.
                  </Text>
                </Banner>
              </BlockStack>
            </Card>
          </Layout.Section>

          {/* ----------------------------------------------------------------
              Section 4: Still need help?
          ---------------------------------------------------------------- */}
          <Layout.Section>
            <Card>
              <BlockStack gap="400">
                <Text as="h2" variant="headingMd">
                  Still need help?
                </Text>
                <Divider />
                <Text as="p" tone="subdued" variant="bodyMd">
                  Can’t find what you’re looking for? Our support team is
                  always ready to help you succeed with Zip Code Checker.
                </Text>
                <InlineStack gap="300" wrap>
                  <Button
                    url="https://docs.zipcodechecker.app"
                    external
                  >
                    Documentation
                  </Button>
                  <Button
                    url="mailto:support@boldteq.com"
                    external
                    variant="primary"
                  >
                    Email Support
                  </Button>
                  <Button
                    url="https://feedback.zipcodechecker.app"
                    external
                  >
                    Feature Requests
                  </Button>
                </InlineStack>
              </BlockStack>
            </Card>
          </Layout.Section>

        </Layout>
      </Box>
    </Page>
  );
}

export function ErrorBoundary() {
  return boundary.error(useRouteError());
}

export const headers: HeadersFunction = (headersArgs) => {
  return boundary.headers(headersArgs);
};

Build a complete Feature Requests page for the Zip Code Checker Shopify app. This is an in-app feature request/feedback board where shop owners can suggest and vote on features.

## What to build

### 1. Prisma Schema — Add two new models to `prisma/schema.prisma`:

```prisma
model FeatureRequest {
  id          String   @id @default(cuid())
  title       String
  description String
  category    String   @default("General")
  status      String   @default("under_review") // under_review, planned, in_progress, done, shipped
  shop        String   // who submitted it
  votesCount  Int      @default(0) // denormalized vote count for sorting
  createdAt   DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt   DateTime @updatedAt
  votes       FeatureVote[]

  @@index([status])
  @@index([votesCount])
}

model FeatureVote {
  id               String         @id @default(cuid())
  featureRequestId String
  shop             String
  createdAt        DateTime       @default(now())
  featureRequest   FeatureRequest @relation(fields: [featureRequestId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@unique([featureRequestId, shop])
  @@index([shop])
}
```

### 2. Run the migration
After updating schema.prisma, run: `npx prisma migrate dev --name add-feature-requests`

### 3. Create route `app/routes/app.feature-requests.tsx`

This should follow all existing patterns from CLAUDE.md. Here's the full spec:

**Loader:**
- `authenticate.admin(request)` 
- Fetch all FeatureRequests with vote count
- Check which ones the current shop has voted for
- Return features, shop name, stats

**Action (intents):**
- `submit` — create a new FeatureRequest (title, description, category required)
- `vote` — toggle vote on a feature request (upvote if not voted, remove vote if already voted). Update the denormalized votesCount.
- `delete` — delete own feature request (only if shop matches)

**Component UI (Polaris v13 ONLY):**

The page should look premium and polished like the screenshot reference:

1. **Page header**: Title "Feature Requests", subtitle "Vote on features or suggest new ones. We review every request and ship based on community votes."
   - backAction to /app
   - primaryAction: "Suggest a Feature" button that opens a modal

2. **Stats bar** (like waitlist page): 
   - Total requests count
   - Under Review count  
   - Planned count
   - In Progress count
   - Done/Shipped count

3. **Filter tabs** using Polaris `Tabs` component:
   - All, Under Review, Planned, In Progress, Done
   - Each tab shows count badge

4. **Sort dropdown**: "Most Voted" (default), "Newest", "Oldest"

5. **Feature request cards** — each card shows:
   - Vote button on the left (upvote arrow + count). If the current shop has voted, show it as active/primary tone
   - Title (bold)
   - Description (truncated to 2 lines with "View details" link)
   - Status badge (color-coded: under_review=attention, planned=info, in_progress=warning, done=success)
   - Category badge
   - Date submitted
   - If the current shop submitted it, show a delete button

6. **Suggest a Feature modal:**
   - Title (TextField, required)
   - Description (TextField multiline, required)  
   - Category (Select: General, UI & Design, Data & Export, API & Integration, Performance, Billing)
   - Submit button

7. **Empty state** when no features match filter

8. **Pagination** — 10 items per page

**Important implementation details:**
- Use `useFetcher` for all actions (vote, submit, delete)
- Show toast on success actions
- The vote button should be optimistic — update UI immediately before server responds
- Use proper Polaris components: Page, Layout, Card, BlockStack, InlineStack, Text, Button, Badge, Tabs, Select, TextField, Modal, EmptyState, Box, Divider, Icon, Banner, Tooltip
- Import icons from @shopify/polaris-icons as needed
- Add loading states
- Handle errors with Banner inside modal
- Use `useAppBridge` for toasts

### 4. Update navigation in `app/routes/app.tsx`
Add a nav link for Feature Requests between "Help & Support" and before the closing tag:
```
<s-link href="/app/feature-requests">Feature Requests</s-link>
```

### 5. Update the help page link
In `app/routes/app.help.tsx`, change the Feature Requests button from external URL to internal navigation:
```tsx
<Button
  url="/app/feature-requests"
>
  Feature Requests
</Button>
```
Remove the `external` prop.

### 6. Run typecheck
After everything is done, run `npm run typecheck` and fix ALL errors.

## Code quality requirements:
- Follow ALL patterns from CLAUDE.md
- TypeScript everywhere, no `any` types
- Error handling on every async operation
- Only Polaris v13 components
- Match the exact patterns from existing routes like app.waitlist.tsx

## Reference files to read first:
- `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Shopify App/Zip-Code/CLAUDE.md`
- `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Shopify App/Zip-Code/prisma/schema.prisma`

Build everything and make sure typecheck passes.

Build a complete Feature Requests page for the Zip Code Checker Shopify app. This is an in-app feature request/feedback board where shop owners can suggest and vote on features.

## What to build

### 1. Prisma Schema — Add two new models to `prisma/schema.prisma`:

```prisma
model FeatureRequest {
  id          String   @id @default(cuid())
  title       String
  description String
  category    String   @default("General")
  status      String   @default("under_review") // under_review, planned, in_progress, done, shipped
  shop        String   // who submitted it
  votesCount  Int      @default(0) // denormalized vote count for sorting
  createdAt   DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt   DateTime @updatedAt
  votes       FeatureVote[]

  @@index([status])
  @@index([votesCount])
}

model FeatureVote {
  id               String         @id @default(cuid())
  featureRequestId String
  shop             String
  createdAt        DateTime       @default(now())
  featureRequest   FeatureRequest @relation(fields: [featureRequestId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@unique([featureRequestId, shop])
  @@index([shop])
}
```

### 2. Run the migration
After updating schema.prisma, run: `npx prisma migrate dev --name add-feature-requests`

### 3. Create route `app/routes/app.feature-requests.tsx`

This should follow all existing patterns from CLAUDE.md. Here's the full spec:

**Loader:**
- `authenticate.admin(request)` 
- Fetch all FeatureRequests with vote count
- Check which ones the current shop has voted for
- Return features, shop name, stats

**Action (intents):**
- `submit` — create a new FeatureRequest (title, description, category required)
- `vote` — toggle vote on a feature request (upvote if not voted, remove vote if already voted). Update the denormalized votesCount.
- `delete` — delete own feature request (only if shop matches)

**Component UI (Polaris v13 ONLY):**

The page should look premium and polished like the screenshot reference:

1. **Page header**: Title "Feature Requests", subtitle "Vote on features or suggest new ones. We review every request and ship based on community votes."
   - backAction to /app
   - primaryAction: "Suggest a Feature" button that opens a modal

2. **Stats bar** (like waitlist page): 
   - Total requests count
   - Under Review count  
   - Planned count
   - In Progress count
   - Done/Shipped count

3. **Filter tabs** using Polaris `Tabs` component:
   - All, Under Review, Planned, In Progress, Done
   - Each tab shows count badge

4. **Sort dropdown**: "Most Voted" (default), "Newest", "Oldest"

5. **Feature request cards** — each card shows:
   - Vote button on the left (upvote arrow + count). If the current shop has voted, show it as active/primary tone
   - Title (bold)
   - Description (truncated to 2 lines with "View details" link)
   - Status badge (color-coded: under_review=attention, planned=info, in_progress=warning, done=success)
   - Category badge
   - Date submitted
   - If the current shop submitted it, show a delete button

6. **Suggest a Feature modal:**
   - Title (TextField, required)
   - Description (TextField multiline, required)  
   - Category (Select: General, UI & Design, Data & Export, API & Integration, Performance, Billing)
   - Submit button

7. **Empty state** when no features match filter

8. **Pagination** — 10 items per page

**Important implementation details:**
- Use `useFetcher` for all actions (vote, submit, delete)
- Show toast on success actions
- The vote button should be optimistic — update UI immediately before server responds
- Use proper Polaris components: Page, Layout, Card, BlockStack, InlineStack, Text, Button, Badge, Tabs, Select, TextField, Modal, EmptyState, Box, Divider, Icon, Banner, Tooltip
- Import icons from @shopify/polaris-icons as needed
- Add loading states
- Handle errors with Banner inside modal
- Use `useAppBridge` for toasts

### 4. Update navigation in `app/routes/app.tsx`
Add a nav link for Feature Requests between "Help & Support" and before the closing tag:
```
<s-link href="/app/feature-requests">Feature Requests</s-link>
```

### 5. Update the help page link
In `app/routes/app.help.tsx`, change the Feature Requests button from external URL to internal navigation:
```tsx
<Button
  url="/app/feature-requests"
>
  Feature Requests
</Button>
```
Remove the `external` prop.

### 6. Run typecheck
After everything is done, run `npm run typecheck` and fix ALL errors.

## Code quality requirements:
- Follow ALL patterns from CLAUDE.md
- TypeScript everywhere, no `any` types
- Error handling on every async operation
- Only Polaris v13 components
- Match the exact patterns from existing routes like app.waitlist.tsx

## Reference files to read first:
- `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Shopify App/Zip-Code/CLAUDE.md`
- `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Shopify App/Zip-Code/prisma/schema.prisma`
- `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Shopify App/Zip-Code/app/routes/app.tsx`
- `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Shopify App/Zip-Code/app/routes/app.help.tsx`
- `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Shopify App/Zip-Code/app/routes/app.waitlist.tsx` (for patterns)
- `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Shopify App/Zip-Code/app/db.server.ts`

Build everything and make sure typecheck passes.

model ShopSettings {
  id                String   @id @default(cuid())
  shop              String   @unique
  defaultBehavior   String   @default("block") // "block" = block all unlisted zips, "allow" = allow all unlisted zips
  notificationEmail String?  // email to receive waitlist notifications
  createdAt         DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt         DateTime @updatedAt
}

model FeatureRequest {
  id          String        @id @default(cuid())
  title       String
  description String
  category    String        @default("General")
  status      String        @default("under_review") // under_review, planned, in_progress, done, shipped
  shop        String        // who submitted it
  votesCount  Int           @default(0) // denormalized vote count for sorting
  createdAt   DateTime      @default(now())
  updatedAt   DateTime      @updatedAt
  votes       FeatureVote[]

  @@index([status])
  @@index([votesCount])
}

model FeatureVote {
  id               String         @id @default(cuid())
  featureRequestId String
  shop             String
  createdAt        DateTime       @default(now())
  featureRequest   FeatureRequest @relation(fields: [featureRequestId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@unique([featureRequestId, shop])
  @@index([shop])
}

Review the most recent changes in the Zip Code Checker Shopify app. ## Review Strategy This is the quality gate. Run this after any feature build or bug fix to catch regressions and ensure Shopify ecosystem compliance. ### Phase 1 — Automated Checks Run these commands first and report results: 1. `npm run typecheck` — must be ZERO errors 2. `npm run lint` — check for linting issues ### Phase 2 — Security Audit (Critical — Report Every Violation) #### Auth & Data Isolation 1. **Auth missing** — any `app.*` route without `authenticate.admin(request)` at the top of loader/action 2. **Cross-shop data leak** — any DB query missing `where: { shop: session.shop }` 3. **Public route with admin auth** — any `api.*` route that accidentally uses `authenticate.admin` 4. **Exposed secrets** — any session tokens, API keys, or internal IDs in public API responses #### Input Validation 5. **Unsanitized input** — public API endpoints without `shop` parameter validation 6. **Missing CORS** — public API responses without `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` headers 7. **SQL/Prisma injection** — user input passed directly to queries without sanitization ### Phase 3 — Shopify Ecosystem Compliance #### Architecture 1. **Shopify API in components** — any GraphQL/REST calls outside loader/action functions 2. **Raw fetch for Shopify API** — using `fetch()` instead of `admin.graphql()` from authenticated client 3. **Missing idempotency** — webhook handlers that don't check for existing records before creating #### Polaris v13 Compliance 4. **Raw HTML layout** — `
`, `

`, `

`, `` used instead of Polaris components 5. **Missing loading states** — forms that submit without SkeletonPage during navigation 6. **Missing empty states** — list/table views without EmptyState component for zero items 7. **Missing Toast feedback** — mutations (create/update/delete) without success/error Toast 8. **Missing error Banner** — actions without try/catch or without error display to user #### Billing 9. **Ungated premium features** — features that should check subscription plan but don't 10. **Direct billing API calls** — billing logic outside of `billing.server.ts` ### Phase 4 — Code Quality 1. **TypeScript `any`** — any explicit `any` type or unsafe type assertion 2. **Console.log in production** — any `console.log` left in committed code 3. **TODO/FIXME comments** — any placeholder comments that should have been resolved 4. **Hardcoded values** — shop names, API keys, or test data in production code 5. **Remix imports** — imports from `@remix-run/react` instead of `react-router` 6. **Missing error handling** — async operations without try/catch ### Phase 5 — API Contract Validation (If Public APIs Changed) - Verify response shapes match documented contracts - Verify error responses include proper status codes and messages - Verify CORS headers on all responses including errors - Verify shop parameter validation on every endpoint ## Output Format ``` ## Review Results ### Automated Checks - TypeCheck: PASS/FAIL (X errors) - Lint: PASS/FAIL (X warnings) ### Critical Issues (Must Fix) [numbered list — file:line, what's wrong, how to fix] ### Quality Issues (Should Fix) [numbered list — file:line, what's wrong, how to fix] ### Billing/Plan Issues [numbered list or "None found"] ### Summary - Total critical: X - Total quality: X - Recommendation: [SHIP IT / FIX CRITICAL FIRST / NEEDS REWORK] ``` ## Files to Check Focus on recently modified files (use `git diff` and `git status`). Also spot-check: - Any new `app.*.tsx` routes - Any new `api.*.tsx` routes - Any changes to `prisma/schema.prisma` - Any changes to `billing.server.ts` or `plans.ts` - Any changes to widget-related files ## Collaboration - If critical issues found → recommend `/fix [issue description]` to route to bug-fixer - If missing features found → recommend `/feature [description]` to route to builder - If widget issues found → flag for widget-specialist agent

content.text:
## Review Results

### Automated Checks
- **TypeCheck:** PASS (0 errors)
- **Lint:** PASS (0 warnings)

### Critical Issues (Must Fix)

**1. Vote race condition — non-atomic count update** ([app.feature-requests.tsx:125-157](app/routes/app.feature-requests.tsx#L125-L157))

The vote action reads `feature.votesCount`, then separately updates it. If two shops vote simultaneously, the count can be wrong. Should use Prisma `increment`/`decrement` instead.

**2. No rate limiting / spam protection on submit** ([app.feature-requests.tsx:102-119](app/routes/app.feature-requests.tsx#L102-L119))

A shop can submit unlimited feature requests with no throttle. Should limit per-shop submissions (e.g., max 10 active requests per shop).

**3. No description length validation** ([app.feature-requests.tsx:104](app/routes/app.feature-requests.tsx#L104))

Title is capped at 150 chars, but description has no max length. A user could submit megabytes of text.

## FEATURE REQUESTS PAGE — FULL ANALYSIS

### 1. LOADER/ACTION CODE OVERVIEW

**Loader (lines 59-86):**
- Authenticates with `authenticate.admin(request)`
- Fetches ALL features (no pagination at DB level — loads everything into memory)
- Fetches user's voted feature IDs in parallel with `Promise.all()`
- Calculates stats by filtering in-memory (total, under_review, planned, in_progress, done)
- Returns: `{ features, votedIds, shop, stats }`

**Action (lines 92-186):**
- Authenticates first, extracts `shop` from session
- Routes to 3 intents via `formData.get("intent")`
  - **submit** (lines 102-119): Creates FeatureRequest, validates title/description length
  - **vote** (lines 121-160): Toggle vote via FeatureVote unique constraint, updates denormalized `votesCount`
  - **delete** (lines 162-176): Owner-only, deletes FeatureRequest (cascades to votes via Prisma)
- All operations wrapped in try/catch, returns `ActionResult` union type
- No pagination filtering — all features loaded then sorted/sliced client-side

---

### 2. STATE MANAGEMENT PATTERNS

**Three layers of state:**

| Layer | State | Type | Purpose |
|-------|-------|------|---------|
| **Loader** | `features`, `votedIds`, `shop`, `stats` | Async data | Initial render data |
| **Optimistic** | `optimisticVotes` Map<string, {count, voted}> | Local state | Instant vote feedback before server response |
| **UI State** | `selectedTab`, `sortValue`, `currentPage`, `modalOpen`, `expandedIds` | Local state | Filter/sort/pagination/modal control |
| **Form State** | `newTitle`, `newDescription`, `newCategory` | Local state | Controlled inputs in submit modal |
| **Loading** | `pendingVoteId`, `pendingDeleteId`, `isSubmitting` | Local state | Per-card spinner flags |
| **Refs** | `pendingIntentRef`, `pendingFeatureIdRef`, `pendingDeleteIdRef` | useRef | Track pending operation context for useEffect |

**Vote flow:**
1. Click vote → optimistic update (Map + Set)
2. Submit via single fetcher
3. useEffect watches `fetcher.data` → confirms/rolls back optimistic state
4. Vote button shows loading state via `pendingVoteId === feature.id && fetcher.state !== "idle"`

---

### 3. PRISMA MODELS

**FeatureRequest (lines 150-164):**
```prisma
model FeatureRequest {
  id          String        @id @default(cuid())
  title       String
  description String
  category    String        @default("General")
  status      String        @default("under_review")
  shop        String        // who submitted it
  votesCount  Int           @default(0) // DENORMALIZED for sorting
  createdAt   DateTime      @default(now())
  updatedAt   DateTime      @updatedAt
  votes       FeatureVote[]

  @@index([status])
  @@index([votesCount])
}
```

**FeatureVote (lines 166-175):**
```prisma
model FeatureVote {
  id               String         @id @default(cuid())
  featureRequestId String
  shop             String
  createdAt        DateTime       @default(now())
  featureRequest   FeatureRequest @relation(fields: [featureRequestId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@unique([featureRequestId, shop])  // ONE vote per shop per feature
  @@index([shop])
}
```

**Key design:**
- FeatureVote enforces `UNIQUE(featureRequestId, shop)` — idempotent voting
- Delete cascades via `onDelete: Cascade`
- `votesCount` is denormalized (updated manually in action)
- No relation backref in FeatureVote to FeatureRequest props

---

### 4. UNUSED REFS & DEAD CODE

**Unused references:**
- Line 271-273: `pendingIntentRef`, `pendingFeatureIdRef`, `pendingDeleteIdRef` — these refs track pending operations but are ONLY used to pass data to the useEffect (line 323). They could be replaced by `fetcher.formData`, but TypeScript doesn't infer the narrow type safely, so refs work around this.
- Actually NOT dead — they're intentional workarounds. See comment on lines 269-270.

**Unused imports:**
- None detected. All imports are used.

**Unused constants:**
- None. CATEGORY_OPTIONS, STATUS_LABELS, STATUS_TONES, SORT_OPTIONS all used.

**Dead code:**
- None found.

---

### 5. SINGLE FETCHER USAGE

**One `fetcher` handles all 3 intents:**

```javascript
const fetcher = useFetcher<typeof action>();
```

**Vote (lines 459-462):**
```javascript
const fd = new FormData();
fd.set("intent", "vote");
fd.set("featureId", featureId);
fetcher.submit(fd, { method: "POST" });
```

**Delete (lines 473-476):**
```javascript
const fd = new FormData();
fd.set("intent", "delete");
fd.set("id", id);
fetcher.submit(fd, { method: "POST" });
```

**Submit (lines 490-495):**
```javascript
const fd = new FormData();
fd.set("intent", "submit");
fd.set("title", newTitle.trim());
fd.set("description", newDescription.trim());
fd.set("category", newCategory);
fetcher.submit(fd, { method: "POST" });
```

**Response handling (lines 319-372):**
- Single useEffect watches `fetcher.state` and `fetcher.data`
- Discriminates via `"error" in data` and `data.intent`
- Uses refs to know which operation was pending when response arrived
- Toast for vote/delete, modal Banner for submit errors

**Issue:** If two requests fire in quick succession, the second overwrites the ref tracking. This is a race condition risk for concurrent submissions.

---

### 6. VALIDATION LOGIC

**What's validated:**

| Validation | Where | Scope |
|------------|-------|-------|
| `intent` required | action line 98 | Coerced to string, no missing check |
| `featureId` required (vote) | action line 123 | Checked, error if empty |
| Feature exists (vote) | action line 125 | DB query, error if not found |
| Owner check (delete) | action line 170 | `toDelete.shop !== shop` |
| Title non-empty | action line 107 + component line 482 | Both client AND server |
| Description non-empty | action line 107 + component line 482 | Both client AND server |
| Title length ≤ 150 | action line 110 + component line 886 | Server enforced, UI maxLength |
| Category required | action line 105 | Defaults to "General" if missing |

**What's MISSING validation:**
- Description length cap (no server or client-side limit)
- Category enum validation (accepts any string, should whitelist CATEGORY_OPTIONS)
- XSS prevention (title/description stored as-is, rendered in Text component — but Polaris escapes by default)
- Duplicate feature detection (same shop can submit identical features)
- Rate limiting (no submission throttle per shop)
- Title/description whitespace-only check (`.trim()` used but `!title.trim()` would catch it)

---

### 7. PAGINATION PATTERN

**Type:** Client-side only

**How it works (lines 406-413):**
```javascript
const totalPages = Math.ceil(filteredFeatures.length / PAGE_SIZE);
const paginatedFeatures = useMemo(() => {
  const start = (currentPage - 1) * PAGE_SIZE;
  return filteredFeatures.slice(start, start + PAGE_SIZE);
}, [filteredFeatures, currentPage]);
```

**Flow:**
1. Loader fetches ALL features (no `take`/`skip` in DB query)
2. Component filters by tab + sorts (in-memory)
3. Component slices to PAGE_SIZE (10 items) based on `currentPage` state
4. Pagination buttons on lines 830-849

**Problems:**
- If shop has 10,000 features, ALL load into memory every request
- No cursor-based pagination or DB-level `take`/`skip`
- Sorting happens after load (O(n log n) per render)
- Stats recalculated on every render (should memoize)

**Recommendation:**
Server-side pagination via `take(PAGE_SIZE).skip((page - 1) * PAGE_SIZE)` in loader.

| **Auth** | ✅ `authenticate.admin()` called in both loader + action |
| **DB Model** | ✅ Proper unique constraint, cascade delete, denormalized votesCount |

| **Error handling** | ✅ Try/catch in action, toasts/banners in component |

- `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Shopify App/Zip-Code/prisma/schema.prisma` — FeatureRequest + FeatureVote models

## Context

# Fix Feature Requests Page — Critical Issues from Review

## Context
The Feature Requests page (`app/routes/app.feature-requests.tsx`) was built and works well in the UI, but a code review found 7 issues (5 critical, 2 quality). This plan addresses all of them in the single route file — no schema changes needed.

## File to modify
- `app/routes/app.feature-requests.tsx`

## Fixes

### 1. Atomic vote counts (Critical)
**Problem:** Vote action reads `feature.votesCount`, then updates it separately — race condition if two shops vote simultaneously.
**Fix:** Replace manual read+write with Prisma `increment`/`decrement`:
```ts
// Instead of: newCount = feature.votesCount + 1; update({ votesCount: newCount })
// Use: update({ votesCount: { increment: 1 } })
```
Then read back the updated record to get the actual `newCount`.

### 2. Per-shop submission limit (Critical)
**Problem:** A shop can submit unlimited feature requests.
**Fix:** Before creating, count existing requests from this shop. Cap at 20 per shop. Return error if exceeded.

### 3. Description max length validation (Critical)
**Problem:** Title capped at 150 chars, but description has no limit.
**Fix:** Add server-side validation: `description.length > 2000` → error. No UI change needed (multiline TextField naturally limits input).

### 4. Remove dead refs (Critical)
**Problem:** `pendingFeatureIdRef` and `pendingDeleteIdRef` are written to but never read.
**Fix:** Remove both refs. Keep only `pendingIntentRef` (which IS read in the useEffect at line 323).

### 5. Category whitelist validation (Quality)
**Problem:** Server accepts any arbitrary category string.
**Fix:** Add `VALID_CATEGORIES` set, validate `category` against it in the `submit` action. Fall back to "General" if invalid.

### 6. Separate fetchers for independent actions (Quality)
**Problem:** Single `useFetcher` shared across vote/delete/submit — concurrent actions can cancel each other.
**Fix:** Use 3 separate fetchers:
- `voteFetcher` — for vote toggle
- `deleteFetcher` — for delete
- `submitFetcher` — for new feature submission

Update the useEffect response handlers to watch each fetcher independently.

### 7. Server-side pagination (Critical — deferred)
**Problem:** Loader fetches ALL features with no limit.
**Fix:** Keep client-side pagination for now (feature request boards rarely exceed hundreds of items across all shops), but add a safety cap: `take: 500` in the DB query to prevent unbounded growth. Full server-side pagination would require URL search params and significantly more complexity — not worth it for this use case yet.

## Verification
1. `npm run typecheck` — must pass with 0 errors
2. Test voting: click vote, verify count updates instantly (optimistic), confirm server syncs
3. Test rapid voting on different features — no cancellation
4. Test submit while vote is in-flight — both should complete independently
5. Test submitting 21st feature request — should show error
6. Test submitting with >2000 char description — should show error
7. Test submitting with invalid category via devtools — should default to "General"

A single `ICONS` object defined once with 13 named SVG strings: `location`, `search`, `check`, `xCircle`, `truck`, `calendar`, `clock`, `card`, `refresh`, `mail`, `users`, `spinner`, `checkmark`. All use the same stroke/outlined style at a 24x24 viewBox — consistent with the existing heading icon. The spinner uses a `zcc-spin` CSS animation.

**2. Button structure — "CHECK X" bug fixed**

The check button HTML was changed from a flat SVG + escaped label string to a two-span structure: `<span class="zcc-btn-icon">` + `<span class="zcc-btn-label">`. The old approach set `btn.textContent = "…"` during loading, which destroyed the inner SVG. Now `setBtnLoading(true/false)` targets each span independently — the icon swaps to the animated spinner and the label swaps to `…`, then both restore precisely. The `btnOrigHtml` variable and `btn.innerHTML = btnOrigHtml` pattern are completely removed.

**3. All emoji/Unicode character replacements**

- Social proof text: `'\uD83D\uDE4B Join N others…'` replaced with DOM element construction using `ICONS.users` SVG inside a `.zcc-social-proof-icon` span
- Waitlist success: `'\u2713 Your request…'` replaced with a `.zcc-wl-success` div using `ICONS.checkmark`
- All result icons now reference `ICONS.check`, `ICONS.xCircle`
- All meta rows (ETA, zone, days, cutoff, COD, return policy) use `ICONS.truck`, `ICONS.calendar`, `ICONS.clock`, `ICONS.card`, `ICONS.refresh`
- Waitlist toggle button uses `ICONS.mail`
- Waitlist submit button uses `ICONS.mail` with the same icon/label span structure as the main check button

**4. CSS updates in `buildSharedCss`**

- Added `@keyframes zcc-spin` for the spinner animation
- Added `.zcc-btn-icon` / `.zcc-btn-label` rules with proper sizing (`svg` at 15x15)
- Added `display:block` to all SVGs to prevent inline baseline gap
- Meta row SVGs: explicit `width`/`height` 14px with `opacity:0.7` for visual hierarchy
- Cutoff/days rows: 13px icons with `opacity:0.6` (secondary info)
- Removed `.zcc-meta .zcc-emoji` class (no longer needed)
- Added `.zcc-result-message` with `font-weight:600`
- Added `.zcc-wl-btn-icon` / `.zcc-wl-btn-label` styles and `display:flex` on `.zcc-wl-btn`
- Added `.zcc-wl-success` and `.zcc-wl-success-icon` styles with `successColor`
- Added `.zcc-social-proof-icon` with proper SVG sizing
- COD badge: slightly increased alpha values for better visibility

**5. CSS updates in `buildWidgetCss`**

- Result icon SVG colors explicitly set via `stroke:` for `.zcc-result.ok` (success color) and `.zcc-result.fail` (error color) — icons now match the card's semantic color rather than inheriting neutral text color
- Waitlist form inputs now have explicit `background:#fff` and `color` to prevent theme interference
- Waitlist button gets `padding:10px 16px` and `letter-spacing:0.01em` for better text rendering
- `aria-live="polite"` added to the result container for screen reader announcements

content.text: Here is the complete audit of `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Shopify App/Zip-Code/extensions/zip-code-widget/blocks/zip-code-checker.liquid`. --- ## Audit Results ### 1. Remaining Emojis / Unicode Symbols No emoji characters remain anywhere in the file. All visual elements use SVG icons. The only Unicode escapes present are: - Line 172: `\u2019` — a right single quotation mark (typographic apostrophe in "don\u2019t"). This is correct typography, not a visual icon. - Line 491: `\u2026` — horizontal ellipsis in the loading button label "Submitting\u2026". This is a text character used as a label suffix, not an emoji. - Line 536: `\u00b7` — middle dot used as a separator between delivery days (e.g. "Mon · Wed · Fri"). Typographic separator, not an emoji. - Line 600: `\u2026` in the social proof text — wait, actually line 600 is `' Join ' + count + ' other' + ...` with no Unicode escape. That is clean. - Line 696: `'Submitting\u2026'` — ellipsis, same as above. Fine. All clean on emojis. --- ### 2. "CHECK X" Button — Reset/Clear Icon There is no "X" button on the input field at all. The widget does not implement any clear/reset input icon. The button shows: - Default state: search icon + button text (lines 463–465) - Loading state: spinner icon + ellipsis text (lines 489–490) - After result: it resets back to search icon + `cfg.buttonText` (lines 492–494) There is no state where the button shows a text "X". The user's concern about "CHECK X" is not present — but there is also no per-result "clear/reset" affordance. After a ZIP check returns a result (success or failure), the button reverts to the search icon + original label. If the intent was for the button to show a reset-to-clear icon after a result is displayed, that functionality is absent entirely. --- ### 3. Delivery Timeline (ORDER → SHIPS → DELIVER) There is no ORDER → SHIPS → DELIVER timeline component anywhere in the file. The file renders delivery info as individual metadata rows (`zcc-meta` divs) with truck, calendar, and clock icons. No timeline/stepper UI exists. If this was a feature that was supposed to be in the widget, it is not present. --- ### 4. Social Proof Text Line 600: `' Join ' + count + ' other' + (count !== 1 ? 's' : '') + ' waiting for delivery to your area'` The SVG icon used is `ICONS.users` (a people/group icon, line 599). No emoji. Clean. One spacing note: on line 600, the text node starts with a space character (` Join ...`). This creates a small gap between the SVG icon and the text, which is intentional since the parent flex container already has `gap:6px` set in the CSS (line 380). The extra leading space on the text node doubles the visual gap between icon and text — it will look slightly wider than expected. This is a minor cosmetic issue but not a bug per se. --- ### 5. COD Available Badge Lines 548–551: ``` ICONS.card + ' Cash on Delivery Available' ICONS.card + ' COD Not Available' ``` The icon is `ICONS.card` (a credit/payment card SVG, line 437). No emoji. Clean. One issue here: The `ICONS.card` SVG is inserted directly adjacent to the text string with a space (`ICONS.card + ' Cash on...'`). This places the SVG and text as raw HTML siblings inside the `zcc-cod` flex container. The CSS sets `gap:5px` on `.zcc-cod` (line 355), so the flex gap handles spacing. However, there is a literal space character between the SVG and the text label in the HTML string. Inside a flex container this space renders as a text node with ~0 visual width (collapsed), so it is harmless — but it is inconsistent with how other icons are wrapped in `` containers. Not a bug, just inconsistency. --- ### 6. Returns Accepted Line 553: `ICONS.refresh + '' + esc(data.returnPolicy) + ''` The icon is `ICONS.refresh` (a circular arrow SVG, line 438). No emoji. Clean. --- ### 7. Loading Spinner Animation Line 441: ``` spinner: '' ``` The `@keyframes zcc-spin` is defined at line 335 in `buildSharedCss`. However, the spinner SVG has `style="animation:zcc-spin 0.8s linear infinite"` hardcoded inline. This style is set at the time the ICONS object is defined (line 441), which is before `buildSharedCss` is called. # Fix & Enhance Feature Requests Page

## Context
The Feature Requests page works well in UI but has critical issues from review + a missing admin capability. Shop owners can submit and vote but nobody can change statuses. Adding admin controls for `zipcodechecker.myshopify.com` only.

## File to modify
- `app/routes/app.feature-requests.tsx` (all changes in this single file)

## Fixes (from review)

### 1. Atomic vote counts
Replace manual read+write with Prisma `increment`/`decrement`. Read back updated record for actual count.

### 2. Per-shop submission limit
Count existing requests from shop before creating. Cap at 20. Return error if exceeded.

### 3. Description max length validation
Server-side: reject if `description.length > 2000`.

### 4. Remove dead refs
Remove `pendingFeatureIdRef` and `pendingDeleteIdRef` (written but never read). Keep `pendingIntentRef`.

### 5. Category whitelist validation
Validate category against `VALID_CATEGORIES` set in submit action. Default to "General" if invalid.

### 6. Separate fetchers
Split single `useFetcher` into 3: `voteFetcher`, `deleteFetcher`, `submitFetcher`. Update useEffect handlers for each.

### 7. Safety cap on DB query
Add `take: 500` to `findMany` in loader to prevent unbounded growth.

## New Feature: Admin Controls

### Admin shop: `zipcodechecker.myshopify.com`

**Loader changes:**
- Pass `isAdmin: shop === "zipcodechecker.myshopify.com"` to the component

**New action intent: `update-status`**
- Only allowed when `shop === "zipcodechecker.myshopify.com"`
- Accepts `id` and `status` (validated against allowed statuses)
- Updates the feature request status

**New action intent: `admin-delete`**
- Only allowed when `shop === "zipcodechecker.myshopify.com"`
- Can delete ANY feature request (not just own)

**UI changes (visible only when `isAdmin === true`):**

## Smart Routing

Before diving in, classify the bug and route to the right agent:

| Bug type | Route to |

| Public API returning wrong data | **widget-specialist** agent |
| CORS / CSP errors | **widget-specialist** agent |
| Polaris component visual bugs | **bug-fixer** agent (Category C) |
| Billing / subscription issues | **bug-fixer** agent (Category G) |
| Complex multi-system bug | Start with **bug-fixer**, hand off as needed |

## Debugging Process (Follow Exactly)

### Step 1 — Locate the Issue
- Find all files related to the error (route file, server file, Prisma schema)
- Read the FULL file where the error originates — understand context before changing anything
- Check the exact error message and stack trace
- Run `npm run typecheck` to see all TypeScript errors at once

### Step 2 — Classify Using Bug-Fixer Categories
Use the bug-fixer agent's diagnostic categories (A through G) to systematically check root causes. The most common:

**Auth issues (70% of Shopify bugs):**
- Is `authenticate.admin(request)` called before every Shopify API usage?
- Is `session.shop` being used to scope DB queries?
- Is the route missing auth (public routes `api.*` should NOT use admin auth)?

**TypeScript errors:**
- Run `npm run typecheck` to see all errors at once
- Check Prisma-generated types match usage
- Check React Router `useLoaderData<typeof loader>()` type inference
- React Router 7 imports from `react-router`, NOT `@remix-run/react`

**Polaris component errors:**
- Check Polaris v13 prop names — many changed from v12
- Check `.d.ts` files in `node_modules/@shopify/polaris/build/ts/src/components/`
- `Badge`/`Banner`: `status` → `tone` in v13

**Prisma/DB errors:**
- Check unique constraints: ZipCode `[shop, zipCode]`, WidgetConfig `shop`
- Use `upsert` for singleton records
- Run `npx prisma migrate dev` if schema changed without migration

**Webhook errors:**
- Must return 200 status always — even on internal errors
- Must be idempotent
- GDPR webhooks: `customers/data_request`, `customers/redact`, `shop/redact`

### Step 3 — Read Before Fixing
Always read the full file before editing. Understand surrounding code context. Match existing patterns exactly.

### Step 4 — Fix (Minimal, Targeted)
- Fix ONLY what is broken — never refactor working code while fixing a bug
- If fixing a TypeScript error, don't change logic
- If fixing a logic bug, don't change types
- Make the smallest change that fixes the issue
- No `// @ts-ignore` or `as any` — fix the root cause

### Step 5 — Verify
- Run `npm run typecheck` — confirm ZERO errors (not just fewer)
- Confirm the fix does not break adjacent functionality
- For Prisma changes: check if migration is needed
- Verify auth scoping is intact

---

## Bug Fix Report

**Root cause**: The widget's zip-check `fetch` chain called `.then(function(r) { return r.json(); })` without checking `r.ok` first. When the production server (Railway) returns a non-JSON response body — such as an HTML 502 Bad Gateway, 503 Service Unavailable, or any gateway-level error page — `r.json()` throws a SyntaxError, which propagates to the `.catch()` handler that displays "Something went wrong. Please try again." Additionally, when the API returns a valid JSON `{ error: "..." }` body (5xx response), the original code would fall through to `esc(data.message)` with `data.message === undefined`, rendering the literal text `"undefined"` in the widget.

**Category**: G-adjacent — public API / widget JavaScript error handling gap

**Files changed**:
- `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Shopify App/Zip-Code/extensions/zip-code-widget/blocks/zip-code-checker.liquid` — lines 509-532 (replaced single `.then(r => r.json())` with a guarded version that handles non-JSON bodies, plus added an early-return guard for `data.error` responses before falling into the normal render path)
- `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Shopify App/Zip-Code/app/routes/api.zip-check.tsx` — line 231 (added `console.error` with shop/zip context in the catch block so production errors appear in Railway logs for diagnosis)

**Fix applied**:
1. The first `.then()` on the zip-check fetch now explicitly checks `r.ok`. If the response is not OK (non-2xx), it attempts `r.json()` and falls back to `{ error: 'Server error (status)' }` if the body is not valid JSON — this prevents `r.json()` from ever throwing and reaching `.catch()`.
2. At the start of the second `.then(data)`, a guard checks `data.error && data.allowed === undefined`. When that condition is true (API returned an error object without an `allowed` field), the widget renders a properly styled error message in the result div and cleans up sessionStorage/custom events, then returns early. The network `.catch()` is now only triggered by genuine network-level failures (no internet, DNS failure), not by server error responses.
3. The API server-side catch block now logs the error with shop/zip context so Railway logs can show what Prisma or other errors are happening in production.

**Verification**: `npm run typecheck` — zero errors. `npm run build` — succeeded cleanly.

**Follow-up needed**: Check Railway logs for `[api.zip-check]` entries after deploying. If you see Prisma errors there, that would indicate the production database is not migrated. Run `npx prisma migrate deploy` against the production DATABASE_URL to ensure all migrations are applied. Also confirm in Railway that the `DATABASE_URL` environment variable is set correctly.
